exposure: Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 anti-spike receptor-binding domain antibody level at delivery
Gestational age at which the last maternal vaccine dose was administered
outcome: Infant SARS-CoV-2 infection under 6 months of age
Neonatal SARS-CoV-2 anti-spike receptor-binding domain antibody level at delivery
cohort: 58 mother-infant dyads were included, whose cord blood sera were tested for SARS-CoV-2 anti-spike antibodies after maternal BNT162b2 vaccination or infection, and infants were followed up for 6 months.
finding: Higher neonatal SARS-CoV-2 anti-spike antibody levels at delivery were associated with a significantly lower likelihood of infant SARS-CoV-2 infection under 6 months of age.
